problem:
Let $V=C[0,2]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,2],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{2}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Calculate the norm of the vector $f(t)=t+{t}^{2}.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Norm of a Vector in Inner Product Spaces

feedback.problem:
Let $V=C[0,1]$ be the vector space of all functions that are continuous on $[0,1],$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩={\int }_{0}^{1}x(t)y(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Normalize the vector $f(t)=t-1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖f(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨f(t),f(t)⟩}.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨f(t),f(t)⟩ & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{(t-1)}^{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\,({t}^{2}-2t+1)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={(\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}-{t}^{2}+t)|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}-1+1 \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
‖f(t)‖=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}.
$$

To normalize the vector $f(t),$ we divide $f(t)$ by its norm $‖f(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\frac{f(t)}{‖f(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{t-1}{(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}})} \\  & =\sqrt{3}(t-1)\end{aligned}
$$
